Mohammad Hossain, Advocate ----- For the Appellant 
Habibul IsLam Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate with Aminul Islam, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.1
parties:
Pubali Bank Ltd ----- Appellant
Vs.
Md Mamunur Rahman and another ----- Respodent
full_judgment:
5. One Shafiul Alam Khan Chowdhury, Manager, Pubali Bank Ltd, Bhairab Bazar Branch, deposed as PW 1 on behalf of the plaintiff. He proved the case of the plaintiff and stated in his examination-in-chief that by a sanction letter dated 16-1-1985 a loan of Taka 8,00,000 was allowed in favour of M/s Sygal Brothers. He proved the sanction letter dated 16-1-1985 (Exhibit 1). He also stated that Md Mamunur Rahman mortgaged his properties mentioned in the second Schedule to the plaint in favour of the bank. Besides, he proved the DP Note, letter of continuity and other charge documents executed by him and the defendant No.2 in favour of the plaintiff bank. Those were marked exhibits. He further stated that on the basis of the application of the defendant dated 15-3-1986 the loan was enhanced to Taka 11,00,000 in favour of the defendant No.1, Taka 9,00,000 by way of cash credit pledge and Taka 2,00,000 by way of hypothecation, on condition that he would keep nuts and tobacco in the godown as pledge against the loan amount of Taka 9,00,000. He also proved the said sanction letters as Exhibit 1 (ka). He further stated that the defendant deposited some amount on 24-6-1986 but since then the defendant did not repay any amount as such, they filed the instant suit praying for a decree for Taka 16, 45,750. He also stated further that in violation of the terms and conditions mentioned in the sanction letter the defendant in collusion with earlier manager illegally kept wheat in the godown instead of the goods to be pledged but as a matter of fact even no wheat was kept in the godown, that because of such reasons, Azizur Rahman, the Manager, was dismissed and he made over his charge on 22-6-1986 in favour of the next manager A Khaleque Jamadar but on 25-6-1986 they received information that Mominur Rahman with the help of this men removed the wheat from his godown, that his was informed to them by godown keeper one Akram Hossain. This witness denied the counter claim and set off raised by the defendant against the plaintiff bank. On recall this witness proved the execution of different charge documents and mortgage deeds executed by the defendant Nos. 1 and 2 in favour of the plaintiff bank. He also proved the letters of the defendant dated 30-8-1986 (Exhibit 17), letter dated 29-10-1986 (Exhibit 17 Ka), the attested copy of the letter of Akram Hossain, godown keeper, dated 26-6-1986 (Exhibit 18) and the letter of the defendant No.1 dated 8-7-1987 (Exhibit 16). In his cross-examination, this witness stated that the mortgagor deposited the deeds of the concerned mortgage properties with the bank, that when the defendant No.2 took loan on 22-3-1983 he deposited the title deeds with the bank but he denied that after repayment of the loan those title deeds were returned to the defendant No. 2, that thereafter the account of Chishty Flour Mills with the plaintiff bank was closed. He further admitted that the agreement between the bank and defendant No. 2 was executed on 28-1-1985 (Exhibit 13), that the said deed was executed by the defendant No.1 although he was not a party to the said deed of agreement. This witness denied the suggestion that the signature of Akhtar Jahan appearing in the deed of agreement was forged. This witness further stated that in violation of the rules, the then Manager allowed loan on the pledge of wheat, that the stock-register shows that there were 1800 bags of wheat on 22-6-1986, that the said quantity of wheat were in the godown of the defendant No.2 under lock and key and guarded by the guards of the bank, that on 22-6-1986, Azizur Rahman handed over charge to Abdul Khaleq Jarnadar, that at the time of handing over it is required to hand over all papers but he did not do so. In his cross-examination he further stated with regard to the removal of the goods from the godown that the incident occurred on 25-6-1986 and the report was given on 26-6-1986, that wheat was not to be kept as pledged rather tobacco and ground nut was required to be kept as pledged, as such, the former manager Azizur Rahman was responsible for keeping the wheat, that the said wheat was stolen during the tenure of manager Khaleque Jamadar, that the key of the godown was kept with Azizur Rahman. He denied that the actual amount of their claim was Taka 9, 13,493 in the two accounts of the defendants and the rest of the claim is interest and other charges. He also denied that the defendant is entitled to damages to the tune of Taka 17,17,100 towards the price of wheat. On recall, the witness produced the stock- register of the pledged goods. He stated that page 80 of the register records the details of the pledged goods of Saigal Brothers from 26-2-1986 to 22-6-1986. Page 80 of the register was marked as Exhibit 19. On his cross-examination, he proved the initials of manager Azizur Rahman, showing receipt of the key by him. 

 6. On behalf of the defendants, the proprietor of the defendant firm, Md Mamunur Rahman deposed as DW 1. In his examination-in-chief he stated that the loan was allowed by sanction letter dated 15-3-1986 for the loan amount of Taka 11,00,000 with condition to keep tobacco and ground nut as pledged with the bank against the loan but since tobacco and wheat was not available in the area he wanted some portion of his loan to purchase those, as such. the manager agreed to allow him loans against pledge of wheat, that the wheat which were pledged was owned by his mother, the defendant No. 2, that the manager received the wheat and kept those under lock and key in the godown, that the godown was under the control of the bank and the key was kept with the manager. After keeping the wheat in the godown, the manager allowed him withdrawal of money towards his loan, that he kept 1800 bags of wheat, each of which weighed two and half maunds,in total 4025 maunds as pledge. that at that time Azizur Rahman Khan was the manager, when he was transferred, he handed over the charge on 22-6-1986 to Abdul Khaleq Jamadar, the new manager, that the manager Azizur Rahman along with other officials in presence of this witness, counted 1,800 bags of wheat and put the godown under lock and key and handed over the same to the new manager. This witness further stated that on 27-6-1986, he asked the new manager to allow him to replace the wheat with tobacco and ground nut and wanted to take back his wheat but at that time the manager informed him that there was no wheat in the godown, that he informed the Chairman of the plaintiff bank by his letter dated 22-7-1986 about such loss of wheat (Exhibit Ka). As such, he incurred a loss of Taka 10,53,000 at the rate of Taka 234 per maund of wheat, the rental of the godown at the rate of Taka 24,000 per year, for four years it came to Taka 96,000, besides, the interest at the rate of Taka 14.5% would have fetched Taka 5,98,700 for the period from 26-6-1986 to 30-9-1989 had the said fund kept in a bank in a fixed deposit, that in total his claim comes to Taka 17,71,100 from the bank. He further stated that on 30-8-1986 the General Manager of the plaintiff bank went there for an enquiry and he found the allegations to be correct and. as such, he proposed to him that if he accepts the loss. the bank will allow him remission of all interest and allow him a further loan of Taka 20,000 as such, he agreed to his proposal that he would repay the loan by monthly installment of Taka 50,000, that ,as such, he wrote a letter on 30-8-1986 (Exhibit 'Ka'(l) to him but subsequently he came to learn that the Board of Directors did not allow him any loan .as such, he renewed his prayer for loan but only an amount of Taka 5,00,000 was sanctioned on 5-2-1987 (Exhibit Kha) but he did not accept the said loan. He further stated that he kept 4500 maunds of wheat as pledge which was misappropriated by the local bank officials and could not return those wheat and he could have repaid the loan had he received back the said wheat, that the bank did not yet hand over the godown in his favour and the same was still under the lock and key of the bank, that the rate of interest was also stipulated arbitrarily in an inflated rate. that the properties mentioned in the first schedule of the plaint belongs to his mother defendant No.2 which was mortgaged to the bank in connection with the loan of Chi sty Flour Mills which was repaid earlier before sanction of the present loan from the plaintiff bank, that on 23,12,1987, he lodged a first information report against the bank and charge sheet was submitted, that his mother, the defendant No. 2 is the owner of the properties mentioned in the 1st schedule to the plaint, that his mother did never mortgage her properties in favour of the plaintiff bank in connection of the present loan taken from the plaintiff bank, that she did not even guarantee the payment of this loan and did not execute any charge documents in favour of the bank, rather the charge documents which were submitted by the bank was executed earlier in connection with the loan allowed in favour of Chishty Flour Mills but the bank used those blank charge documents by filling the blanks in those unfilled charge documents, that his mother was living in America for the last 3/4 years. He denied that the dues of the bank outstanding against him stood at Taka 16,45,750, that he did not fulfill the terms and conditions mentioned in the sanction letter or that in collusion with the earlier manager he illegally kept wheat pledged, that he has no business of wheat and he did not deposit wheat in the godown and that the manager Azizur Rahman did not receive 1800 bags of wheat in his presence on 22-6-1986 then, handed over in favour of the next manager. He denied that on 25-6-1986 his men removed the said wheat from the godown. He denied that his claim of set-off is not correct. In his cross-examination he admitted that his mother was in America for the last 3/4 years, that he took loan by sanction letter dated 16-1-1965 and the endorsement on the other side of the sanction letter is his. He admitted that in the sanction letter it was stipulated that tobacco and ground nut packets would be taken as mortgage against the loan that since Pubali Bank had no godown of its own, he himself rented a godown, the owner of the godown is his mother but the godown was under the control of the bank. He admitted that on 15-3-1986 the loan was enhanced and renewed, that at that time also he did not keep any tobacco or ground nut in the godown, rather he kept wheat there and that on 15-3-1986 he did not inform the head office of the bank about his such storing of wheat instead of ground nut and tobacco. He admitted that generally tobacco comes from North Bengal and per maund of tobacco costs Taka 400 and it costs more to process it. He stated that he did not submit any voucher or receipt to show purchase of wheat, that he does not have any witness showing removal of the wheat from the godown by the bank, that he issued Exhibit 17 and 17Ka. He denied that storage of wheat is imaginary. He denied that Khaleque Jamadar received the wheat in front of him possibly on 22-6-1986. He also said that he has no evidence to show that Khaleque Jamadar received the wheat but volunteered that it is known to officials of the bank. Khaleque Jamadar possibly joined the branch either on 21-6-1986 or 22-6-1986, that he lodged the first information report about the loss of the wheat in December, 1987. He denied that he and his own men removed the wheat had he at all stored there. He admitted that he did not file any separate suit for damages against the plaintiff bank but prayed for set-off but did not yet submit the, court-fees but submitted the challan for the same. 

 7. One Golam Mostafa, the President of the workers union of Bhairab, deposed as PW 2. He stated in his examination-in-chief that he knows the godown where Mamunur Rahman kept his goods mortgaged with the bank, that his office is about 15/20 yards from the said godown and the godown can be seen from his office, that on 25th, June, 1986 he was in his office till morning to evening, that on that date he did not see Mamunur Rahman removing any goods from the said godown. That the godown was under lock and key and was guarded by the darwan of the bank. He was cross- examined but nothing much came out from his cross-examination. One Rais Mia a businessman of kerosene oil deposed as PW 3. He stated in his examination-in-chief that he knows Mamunur Rahman. He also knows the god own where the goods of Saygol Brothers were pledged with the bank. He carries on his business in front of the said godown. On 25th June, 1986 he stayed all day there but never saw Mamunur Rahman or his men to remove any goods from the said godown. He was cross-examined but nothing much came out of his cross-examination. 

 10. We have gone through the plaint, written statements, the deposition of witnesses adduced on behalf of both the parties and also the relevant documents exhibited in this suit. It appears that the suit was filed on 16-2-1988 before the Court of Subordinate Judge, Kishoreganj and was numbered as Money Suit No. 1 of 1988. The defendant filed his first written statement on 26-12-1986 followed by his other additional written statements. Subsequently, on 11-10-1990 it was transferred to the Artha Rin Court and was re-numbered as Artha Rin Case No. 27 of 1990. Thereafter several other additional written statements were submitted on behalf of the defendant. The written statement dated 5-9-1990 gave the details of the counterclaim of Taka 17,71,100 and the court fees on the said amount of counter-claim was deposited on 23-11-1991. On perusal of the written statement, it appears that the defendant No. 1 did not specifically deny either the loan or the claim of the plaintiff bank. The contentions of the defendant No. 1 made in his written statement and three other additional written statements are that he on the permission from Md Azizar Rahman, the then Manager of the plaintiff bank, kept 1800 bags of wheat equivalent to 4500 maunds of wheat, pledged in the godown under the control of the bank against the loan of Taka 11,00,000 enjoyed by him. The value of the said wheat came to Taka 10,76,400 at the rate of Taka .234 per maund of wheat and he is entitled to make the counterclaim in respect of the said amount along with his damages to the extent of Taka 5,98,700 and also the rentals of the godown for the relevant period, as such, according to his written statements, as supported by him in his deposition, comes to Taka 17,71,100 against the claim of the bank. 

 14. The defendants nowhere in his four sets of written statements specifically denied the claim of the plaintiff bank. The bank also proved its claim by adducing evidence which was also accepted to be correct by the Trial Court. The learned Judge however allowed the claim of the bank up to 30-6-1986 and denied the claim of the bank thereafter till February, 1988. No reasoning is found for disallowing the claim of interest of the bank for the said period, perhaps the learned Judge accepting the contention of the defendant that the pledged wheat being removed on or about 26-6-1986; he disallowed the claim of the bank till February, 1988. But the learned Judge did not consider that according to the provisions of the sanction letter Exhibit 1 and 1 Ka, Tobacco and ground nut were stipulated to be pledged with the bank, against the loan allowed by the bank but he apparently in collusion with the local bank manager, in violation of the term of the sanction letter, allegedly kept wheat in the godown. It is also to be noted that the value of the wheat per bag was only Taka 234 whereas the value of the Tobacco even before being processed was Taka 400. So, the defendant No.1 apparently in collusion with local manager, instead of keeping the tobacco and ground nut which were more valuable than wheat, illegally kept the wheat in the godown, if at all, at least on record, beyond the scope of the sanction letter, thereby he himself apparently committed fraud on the bank. Since the loan was not denied, since the loan limit of Taka 11.00 lac was enjoyed by the defendant No. 1 illegally without proper pledge and since the loan was not repaid, we do not see any reason, not to allow the claim of interest of the bank for the rest of the period since July 1987 to February, 1988, for the total amount of Taka 16,45,750 We however, would allow simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum pendent elite till realisation.
